newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's De Beers, Anglo deny Zaire rebel claims.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's De Beers, Anglo deny Zaire rebel claims.

text.p: South African mining giants Anglo American Corp and De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd on Wednesday denied claims by Zairean rebels that they were operating mines in the strife-torn Central African country.
Zairean rebels, who have pushed deeper into the heart of the country, have reassured foreign companies that they will honour mining concessions.
Jean Kabongo, special security adviser to rebel leader Laurent Kabila, said on Tuesday night De Beers and Anglo American had mining operations in areas the rebels now control.
But Anglo American said on Wednesday it had no operations or even exploration teams on the ground in Zaire.
"I can confirm that Anglo has no operations in Zaire at all," Anglo spokeswoman Glenn Finnegan said.
Anglo American chairman Julian Ogilvie-Thompson said last month the company would proceed warily in Zaire and had only submitted a bid to develop the Kolwezi Copper tailings project.
The rebels say that on their southern front they have already captured the mining centre of Kamituga, where they claimed Anglo has been operating.
"We have no operations there and as yet we don't have anybody in the field doing exploration work," Finnegan added.
Industry sources said Canada's Banrow Resources were involved in mining activities in Kamituga.
Anglo has been at the forefront of the move by South African mining houses into Africa since the end of apartheid and is involved in scores of mining projects in other African countries.

De Beers, which controls the world's rough diamond market through its London-based Central Selling Organisation (CSO), said on Wednesday it had no mines in Zaire but maintained about five buying offices in the country.
Kabango said the rebels would try to open up new areas to mining, especially in the central region of Kasai.
"All diamond mines and operations, like De Beers in Mbuji-Mayi, will remain in the hands of the companies who have been running them and operating the franchises up until now".

But De Beers spokesman Tom Tweedy said the company operated no mines in Zaire. Mines were under the control of the state-owned Societe Miniere de Bakwanga (MIBA) which mined Zaire's diamond deposits -- mainly for industrial diamonds.

"De Beers has no diamond mines in Zaire, we don't even have technical guys going up to the MIBA mine. It is a totally separate company run by Zaire and Sibeka in Belgium of which Sibeca only has a 20 percent interest".
He said De Beers had a small stake in Sibeka (SIBEKA Societe D'Enterprises et D'Investissements SA ) but no interest or involvement in the Zaire operations.
"There are 20-odd licensed buying companies in Zaire and we are one of them," Tweedy said.
